title: Fluorescent tagging of endogenous proteins with CRISPR/Cas9 in primary mouse neural stem cells
protocol: Conceptually design the fluorescent tag.
Decide on the placement of the fluorescent tag in the genome.
Identify unique 5′ and 3′ termini for each gene variant if applicable.
Create a minimal disruption fluorescent tag for the protein of interest.
Identify a suitable crRNA to target the site for fluorescent tag knock-in.
Select a suitable fluorescent tag to label the protein of interest.
Design a linker peptide to fuse the protein of interest with the selected fluorescent tag.
Construct a targeting vector encoding the fluorescent tag for tagging the protein of interest.
Select “Single guide” and set guide length to 20.
Choose the correct genome species for your cell type and PAM: NGG.
Click “Finish.”
Identify the specific region of DNA you wish to target by typing in start and end positions or clicking and dragging over the DNA sequence.
Click the green “+” sign to add the selected region.
Select crRNA sequences with the highest “On-Target Score,” aiming for scores above 60.
Choose crRNAs closest to either the 5′ or 3′ end of your gene, depending on which end you are tagging with a fluorescent tag.
Avoid using sgRNAs that cut further than 30 nucleotides from your site of fluorescent tag insertion.
Use a linker peptide between the fluorescent tag and protein of interest to increase proper folding and minimize interference with function and localization.
Choose a linker peptide sequence that is flexible, typically consisting of glycine and serine amino acids (GGGGSGGGGSGGGGS).
Design targeting vector incorporating alternative flexible linker peptides if necessary.
Design the targeting vector DNA sequence containing the desired genomic insert flanked by homologous sequences.
Arrange the linker peptide and fluorescent tag DNA sequences according to their position relative to the protein of interest (amino or carboxyl terminus).
Add at least 500 nucleotides of homologous DNA on either side of the genomic insert sequence.
Consider using shorter homology arms between 50-100 nucleotides if higher efficiency is not a requirement.
Clone the crRNA into the SpCas9:sgRNA dual plasmid.
Order DNA oligonucleotides according to the crRNA design for cloning into the SpCas9:sgRNA dual plasmid backbone.
Digest the template plasmid harboring an empty crRNA cloning site and the SpCas9 sequence with appropriate restriction enzymes.
Prepare the crRNA insert using the ordered DNA oligonucleotides.
Ligate the prepared crRNA insert into the digested plasmid at the empty crRNA cloning site.
Order oligonucleotides with the crRNA sequence and attached nucleotides to create sticky ends for ligation into the linearized SpCas9:sgRNA dual plasmid.

Anneal and phosphorylate the oligos for insertion into the SpCas9:sgRNA dual plasmid in a thermal cycler at 37°C for 30 min, then 95°C for 5 min, decreasing temperature to 25°C at a rate of 5°C per minute.
Restriction digest the SpCas9:sgRNA dual plasmid (pSpCas9(BB)-2A-Puro (PX459) V2.0).
Prepare a restriction digest reaction to linearize the plasmid.
Dephosphorylate the sticky ends in the reaction mixture to prevent self-ligation.
Incubate the reaction mixture for 4 hours at 37°C.
Add 1 μL of shrimp alkaline phosphatase to the reaction after 4 hours.
Incubate the mixture with added phosphatase for an additional hour at 37°C.
Gel purify the linearized plasmid using a QiaQuick Gel Extraction Kit.
Mix crRNA insert and linearized SpCas9:sgRNA dual plasmid for ligation reaction.
Incubate the ligation reaction for 30 minutes at room temperature (25°C).
Thaw 50 μL DH5α on ice for 20 min.
Add 3 μL of the ligation reaction to the DH5α on ice and then let the samples sit on ice for 20 min.
Heat shock samples for 30 s at 42°C.
Place samples back on ice for 2 min after heat shock, add 250 μL SOC recovery media.
Shake samples at 200 rpm at 37°C for 1 h in a bacterial shaker.
Plate 250 μL transformed bacteria onto an LB agar plate with 50 μg/mL ampicillin and grow at 37°C for 18 h.
Screen clones by performing minipreps on clones (Invitrogen R1213).
Perform restriction digests with BbsI to screen clones.
Analyze clones that are not cut with BbsI using Sanger Sequencing to validate insertion of the DNA sequence of the crRNA.
Prepare plasmid DNA for delivery to NSCs by performing an endotoxin-free maxi plasmid purification.
Perform a Gibson Assembly reaction to create a targeting vector plasmid which includes the following sequence: 5′ homology region + linker + mNeon + 3′ homology region.
Perform PCRs to create fragments with overlapping homology to adjacent fragments.
Ligate the resulting fragments into a linearized plasmid to assemble the targeting vector plasmid.
Attach the linker peptide coding sequence to an adjacent fragment, such as the fluorescent tag, prior to Gibson Assembly.
Obtain coding sequences for all components of the designed targeting vector plasmid.
Generate homology arms through PCR using genomic DNA as a template or through commercial DNA synthesis services.
Design primers with a melting temperature greater than 55°C and less than 70°C.
Add a 15–30 nucleotide overhang sequence to each primer for homology to adjacent DNA fragments.
Use the forward primer to amplify the 3′ homology arm, ensuring it contains a 15–30 nucleotide overhang homologous to mNeon.
Use the reverse primer to amplify the 3′ homology arm, ensuring it contains a 15–30 nucleotide overhang homologous to pENTR.
Perform assembly PCR to create an amplicon of the fluorescent tag coding sequence with 15–30 nucleotides of homology to the linker peptide coding sequence.
Perform an assembly PCR using reaction recipe and conditions listed in step 19.
Ligate the fluorescent tag coding sequence with the linker peptide coding sequence.
Attach a 15–30 nucleotide overhang homologous to adjacent fragments in the targeting vector plasmid.
Perform a PCR using the reaction recipe and conditions listed in step 19.
Generate remaining DNA fragments for Gibson Assembly.
Ensure each fragment has a 15–30 nucleotide overhang homologous to adjacent fragments in the targeting vector plasmid.
Amplify DNA fragments from genomic DNA if necessary, adding 0.5 mM MgCl2 and/or 3% dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) to increase amplification success.
Isolate your fragment from genomic DNA after initial PCR amplification.
Perform a second PCR to attach adapter sequences for the Gibson Assembly reaction.
Use other high-fidelity polymerases such as Q5 High-Fidelity DNA Polymerase instead of Phusion.
Gel purify each DNA fragment using Qiagen gel purification kit (Qiagen 28704).
Incubate the restriction digest reaction at 37°C for 1 hour.
Gel purify the linearized plasmid.
Incubate the samples at 50°C for 60 min.
Store samples on ice for same day transformation, or at -20°C for subsequent transformation.
Thaw 50 μL DH5α on ice for 20 min.
Add 2 μL of the ligation reaction to the DH5α on ice and let sit on ice for 20 min.
Heat shock samples for 30 s at 42°C.
Place samples back on ice immediately after heat shock, then add 250 μL SOC recovery media.
Shake samples at 200 rotations per minute at 37°C for 1 h in a bacterial shaker.
Plate 100 μL sample onto an LB agar plate with ampicillin and grow at 37°C for 18 h.
Screen clones for assembly of the targeting vector by PCR colony test, restriction digest, or Sanger sequencing using a sequencing primer ~100 nucleotides upstream of the targeting vector.
Isolate plasmid DNA for delivery to NSCs through endotoxin-free maxi plasmid purification.
Electroporate NSCs with both the SpCas9:sgRNA dual plasmid and the assembled targeting vector plasmid using the Amaxa Nucleofector system.
Culture NSCs for 3–10 days to achieve genetic knock-in of the fluorescent tag coding sequence into the genome and expression of the desired endogenously tagged gene.
Trypsinize adherent proliferating NSCs to generate a single-cell suspension.
Detach any adherent cells from the dish using a pipette.
Create a pellet by centrifuging at 120 × g for 4 min.
Resuspend the pellet in 100 μL of 0.05% trypsin and incubate at 37°C for 5 min.
Quench the trypsinization with 200 μL of trypsin inhibitor.
Mechanically dissociate the sample by pipetting vigorously 15–20 times.
Further quench the trypsinization by adding 3 mL of NSC media DMEM/F12 GlutaMax with penicillin-streptomycin-fungizone, B27, and FGF-2 and EGF.
Remove the trypsin by pelleting the sample through centrifugation at 120 × g for 4 min and aspirating the supernatant.
Count cells using a hemocytometer or cell counter.
Create a pellet of 4 million NSCs through centrifugation at 120 × g for 4 min.
Resuspend the pellet by adding 100 μL Mouse Neural Stem Cell Nucleofector Solution and 3.5 μg SpCas9:sgRNA dual plasmid, pipetting gently up and down 3–5 times.
Add 3.5 μg targeting vector plasmid to the suspension and mix gently up and down 3–5 times.
Transfer resuspension immediately to an electroporation cuvette.
Close the cuvette with the cap.
Electroporate using program A-033 on a Nucleofector device.
Add 1 mL prewarmed NSC media to the cuvette to quench the sample.
Use a plastic disposable pipette to transfer the electroporated cell solutions to a 150 mm diameter uncoated culture dish containing 10 mL of NSC media.
Avoid collecting foam-like cellular debris during transfer.
Return cells to the incubator as quickly as possible.
Trypsinize NSCs and replate them into a 10 cm dish 24 hours following electroporation (optional).
Electroporate NSCs either with or without plasmids for CRISPR/Cas9 mediated tagging of vimentin’s carboxyl terminus with mNeon.
Image tagged NSCs with a fluorescent microscope, with the nucleus labeled with Hoechst (blue).
Analyze single cells using a flow cytometer, measuring mNeon fluorescence and forward scatter-area (FSC-A).
Extract genomic DNA from expanded clones expressing mNeon.
Screen positive clones for homozygous or heterozygous fluorescent tag by PCR.
Precoat a 96-well plate with PLO for 1 hour at 37°C.
Add laminin to the precoated plate and incubate for 3 hours at 37°C.
Trpisinize cells for cell sorting.
Sort single cells using a fluorescence activated cell sorter directly into a 96 well plate preloaded with media.
Resuspend samples in prechilled dPBS with 1 mM EDTA and 1 μg/mL DNAse.
Keep samples on ice until completion of cell sorting.
Spin down the sorted cells in a centrifuge at 120 × g for 4 minutes after sorting.
Change media at least once every 72 hours during cell expansion.
Screen clones with fluorescent tags to identify heterozygous and homozygous knock-ins.
Generate a pellet from at least 10,000 cells for genomic DNA extraction during the first split of cell culture.
Take half of the cells to create a pellet for sequencing and use the other half to continue expanding the clone.
Extract genomic DNA using a commercially available kit (e.g., Thermo Fisher Scientific K182001).
Set up a PCR reaction with primers flanking the site where the fluorescent tag is placed, but outside of homology arms.
Run the PCR products on an agarose gel to visualize and analyze bands indicating alleles harboring or lacking the desired fluorescent tag.
Probe for larger and smaller PCR product bands to determine heterozygous or homozygous clones.
Perform Sanger Sequencing to validate successful placement of the fluorescent tag in the genome without mutations.
